## Contributing atlases to BrainGlobe

Before starting, you will need:
* Information to credit the atlas (publication, website)
* A template reference 3D stack (at least one)
* An annotation 3D stack (at finest level of your region hierarchy)
* A description of all the structures of the brain and their hierarchy.

## How do I contribute an atlas

* Write a [packaging script](https://github.com/brainglobe/brainglobe-atlasapi/tree/main/brainglobe_atlasapi/atlas_generation/atlas_scripts)
* Submit a Pull Request
* Core developers upload to data platform
 
## How are atlases stored?

* On ["GIN" (German Informatics Node)](https://gin.g-node.org/brainglobe/atlases)
  * acts as an archive of atlas data
* improvements (Atlas API V2) in progress
  * use `zarr` to "stream" atlases
  * also avoid data duplication

## Contributing atlases to BrainGlobe {.smaller}

More info on [the BrainGlobe website](https://brainglobe.info/documentation/brainglobe-atlasapi/adding-a-new-atlas.html).
Achievable (?) [hackday idea](https://github.com/orgs/neuroinformatics-unit/projects/19/views/1?pane=issue&itemId=122515055&issue=neuroinformatics-unit%7Cosw25-hackday%7C11):
* Pick an [atlas of interest](https://github.com/brainglobe/brainglobe-atlasapi/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3Anew-atlas)
* Intermediate Python knowledge
* [template script](https://github.com/brainglobe/brainglobe-atlasapi/tree/main/brainglobe_atlasapi/atlas_generation/atlas_scripts/template_script.py) available
* Bonus: improve related documentation
